candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record supports renal sarcoidosis (noncaseating granulomata on renal biopsy, hypercalcemia, suppressed PTH, renal impairment) and the post-resuscitation labs show hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis with hypophosphatemia and hypokalemia consistent with Fanconi syndrome (proximal tubular dysfunction). C001 names the organ-level involvement correctly but does not specify Fanconi syndrome, which is an explicit required component of the benchmark diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Captures sarcoidosis with renal involvement but omits the specific tubular dysfunction component (Fanconi syndrome) required by the benchmark reference

case_quality_flags: Fanconi syndrome evidenced by post-resuscitation hyperchloremic non-anion-gap metabolic acidosis, hypophosphatemia, hypokalemia, and low-normal urea suggesting proximal tubular wasting
Ergocalciferol use noted but PTH suppression and granulomatous 1-alpha-hydroxylation more likely driver of hypercalcemia
Normal chest X-ray does not exclude systemic sarcoidosis; renal biopsy is diagnostic anchor
